wu: Food Charades: Teacher shows flashcards of food, mimes eating it, kids shout 'yum!' or 'yuck!' and guess 'Is it [food]?'
wuAlt: Pass the Plate: Play music, pass a paper plate, stop and child says 'I like [food]' or 'I do not like [food]'.
Flashcard Race: Two teams race to match 'yum!' and 'yuck!' flashcards to food pictures.
pres: Teacher holds up a Ramadan plate with dates, milk, harira, msemen; models 'I like dates. Yum!' and 'I do not like cucumber. Yuck!'; kids repeat, then ask 'Do you like [food]?' to teacher.
presAlt: Storytime: Read 'Samira's Ramadan' book, point to food pictures and ask 'Does Samira like [food]?' kids say 'Yes/No'.
Realia: Bring in suhoor items (bread, cheese) and iftar items (dates, juice), kids touch and say 'I like...'.
prac: Guess the Food: Teams take turns, one child thinks of a food, others ask 'Does he/she like [food]?'; guesser says 'Yes, he does' or 'No, he doesn't' until correct.
pracAlt: Food Survey: Kids walk around with a paper asking 3 friends 'Do you like [food]?' and tally answers with ticks.
Memory Game: Place food cards face down, kids turn two over and say 'I like...' or 'I do not like...' for each.
ls: Listen and Tick: Play a dialogue of two kids talking about food ('Do you like milk?' 'Yes, I do!'); kids listen and tick 'yum' or 'yuck' on their worksheet.
re: Food Relay: Two lines, teacher calls a food, first kid runs to touch the flashcard and shouts 'I like [food]!' or 'I do not like [food]!'.
prod: Iftar Table Craft: Kids draw their family's iftar table, label 5 foods in English, then present to partner 'This is my iftar table. I like... She does not like...'.
rw: Trace and Write: Kids trace 'He likes milk' and 'She does not like bread' sentences, then copy them 3 times; read a short text about Ramadan meals and match foods to 'yum'/'yuck'.
st: Goodbye Song: 'If You're Happy and You Know It' with food verses ('If you like apples, clap your hands!'); sticker chart for participation, high-five line as they exit.
g: Teacher calls 'I like pizza!', kids cover the pizza picture on their bingo card.
Kids find someone who likes a food and say 'Do you like [food]?' then high-five.
Teams race to put food cards in 'yum' or 'yuck' baskets.
Teacher removes a food from a tray, kids guess 'Is it [food]?' with 'Yes/No'.
Child mimes eating and others guess 'Does he/she like [food]?'
diff: Fast finishers: Write 3 more sentences about their family's food likes.
Support: Use word banks with food pictures and 'yum'/'yuck' labels for the craft.
hw: Teach 5 food words to your family and draw their reactions.
Draw your suhoor plate and label 3 foods in English.
Ask your parents about their favorite Ramadan food and write 'He likes...' or 'She likes...'.
tip: Use Ramadan as a bridge to connect the food theme with local culture; praise kids for using full sentences, even if imperfect.
